messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: inference-queue-surge (alert_id=PD-98321). Runbook: AUTOSCALER_LAG -> queue depth > 8000, avg latency > 12000ms. Paging eng-oncall. https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD-98321

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification: alert PD-98321 assigned to olivia (primary).

olivia: Acked. I'm looking. Any customer impact flags?

mike: seeing increased 5xx rate from apps (10m spike). Frontend is returning 503s for some long-running requests. Not full outage but ~6% of requests failing -> a few paying customers reporting errors.

raj: grabbing metrics - k8s HPA shows target CPU at 95%, replicas at 18 (maxed), queue length per dispatcher = 4800, global queue = 8600. Autoscaler logs: `scale_delay: 120s`, last scale event at 1784527200. Looks like spot instance churn earlier caused slow node replacement.

olivia: can we manual-scale to bypass autoscaler slow path? If we can spin nodes to 28 and let dispatcher spin up more workers, should drain.

mike: running: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-worker --replicas=28` now. Also kicking off `nodegroupctl increase --name=spot-inference-pool --count=10` to request 10 nodes.

oncall-coverage-bot: Manual scale request initiated by mike. AWS ASG request id: asg-req-5581. ETA for node ready ~ 90-180s depending on spot placement.

olivia: while nodes come up, please enable temporary routing fallback to dedicated pool for high-priority customers. Sara can you flip the routing policy?

sara: flipping routing for customer_tier=enterprise to dedicated-1 now. Command: `routesctl set-policy --scope=customer_tier=enterprise --route=dedic-1`. Done. Verified 42 sessions moved over, requests for those customers now showing in dedicated pool.

raj: autoscaler logs show repeated preemptions at 1784527000-1784527300 for spot instances in us-west-2. Node startup jitter + image-pull delays made HPA stuck under scale_delay. Also `kvcache` warmup is causing initial requests to be slow, backlog amplifies.

mike: new nodes registering. `kubectl get nodes | grep inference` shows +8 new nodes in Ready state. Scaling worker replicas to 36 to use new capacity. `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-worker --replicas=36`

olivia: good. Monitor queue drain and latency. Raj, can you patch the autoscaler to reduce scale_delay for this pool and add a min-ready buffer?

raj: creating quick patch: set autoscaler config `scale_delay_ms=30000` for spot-inference-pool and `min_reserved_replicas=6`. Pushed config and reloaded service. Will watch for thrash.

pagerduty: PD alert PD-98321 acknowledged by olivia at 1784527902.

mike: queue length trending down: global queue 8600 -> 4200 in 60s, avg latency 12s -> 6s. 5xx rate also decreasing.

olivia: continuing to observe. Sara: leave dedicated routing on for 30m then revert. Also create a temporary incident label for customer comms.

sara: created incident tag `inc-1784527890-warmup-lag`. Notifying support to monitor customer tickets.

oncall-coverage-bot: PagerDuty: escalation timer paused. Current responders: olivia (ack), mike, raj, sara.

raj: noticed a config mismatch in the autoscaler: warm_pool_size was 0 for spot-inference-pool due to a previous cost-savings change. I'm restoring warm_pool_size=4 and adding an alert if warm_pool_size < 2 for production pools.

olivia: great find. Add a task to postmortem: revert cost-savings override, evaluate cost vs risk, and add runbook step to check warm_pool on manifests.

mike: traffic stabilized. Queue at 1200 and dropping, latency ~1.8s tail. Rolling back worker replicas to 24 to avoid overprovisioning. `kubectl scale ... --replicas=24`

olivia: good work. Final actions: 1) leave autoscaler patch in canary for 6h, 2) make warm_pool and min_reserved_replicas part of config defaults, 3) support to send customer notice for impacted tenants. I'll file follow-ups in #postmortems.

sara: support notified. Draft sent to legal for approval; ETA 30m.

olivia: closing on-call thread. If anything spikes, re-open and escalate. Otherwise we'll capture RCA. Thanks team :tada:
